role: Samples host and per-server resource metrics from the kernel, and owns metrics and engine-event history.

fields.label: Log level
fields.description: Minimum severity this leaf logs.

fields.label: Host id
fields.description: Identity this host stores its own metrics under. Defaults to the machine's hostname; it must match the API's host id or history queries return nothing.

fields.label: Sample interval
fields.description: How often the monitor samples host and per-server metrics.

fields.label: Hidden filesystem types
fields.description: Extra filesystem types to leave out of the mount list, on top of the pseudo filesystems that are always filtered.

fields.label: Excluded interface prefixes
fields.description: Interface-name prefixes left out of host network rates, on top of the always-excluded loopback. Virtual-ethernet pairs would otherwise double-count container traffic.

fields.label: Metrics socket
fields.description: Unix socket the monitor serves metrics on. This is the socket the API scrapes.

fields.label: Metrics socket permissions
fields.description: Octal permission bits applied to the metrics socket. The default lets a process in the socket's group scrape it without exposing it host-wide.

fields.label: KGSM executable
fields.description: Path to the KGSM executable. Empty turns per-server sampling off entirely and the monitor reports host metrics only.

fields.label: Instance resync interval
fields.description: How often the monitor re-lists KGSM instances to refresh its watch list. This spawns a process, so it runs well off the metrics tick.

fields.label: Disk footprint interval
fields.description: How often each server's on-disk size is recomputed. This walks the whole instance directory, so it runs on its own slow cadence.

fields.label: Read engine events
fields.description: Tail the engine event journal for sub-second watch-list updates. With this off, per-server metrics still work — the periodic resync remains the source of truth — but engine event history stops being recorded.

fields.label: Engine event journal
fields.description: Directory holding KGSM's append-only event journal, which the monitor tails for engine events. Read-only: the engine is the sole writer, and any number of consumers read the same files with no coordination.

fields.label: Disable metrics history
fields.description: Turn off metrics persistence and the history endpoint. The monitor then serves live frames only, and the Control Panel's metric charts have no data to draw.

fields.label: Metrics database
fields.description: SQLite file holding metrics history. Repointing it starts an empty store and orphans the existing history.

fields.label: Persist interval
fields.description: How often the latest sampled frame is written to history.

fields.label: Raw retention
fields.description: How long full-resolution samples are kept. Also the tier boundary: a query inside this window reads raw samples, one beyond it reads rollups. Lowering it prunes existing rows.

fields.label: Rollup bucket width
fields.description: Width of each aggregated history bucket beyond the raw window.

fields.label: Rollup retention
fields.description: How long aggregated history is kept. Lowering it prunes existing rows.

fields.label: Maintenance interval
fields.description: How often rollup, pruning and vacuuming run over the history store.

fields.label: Disable event history
fields.description: Turn off persistence of KGSM engine events. Independent of metrics history — either can be off without the other. The Control Panel's audit timeline loses its engine-event source.

fields.label: Event database
fields.description: SQLite file holding engine-event history, kept separate from the metrics store so the two never contend for a writer. Repointing it starts empty and orphans the existing history.

fields.label: Event retention
fields.description: How long engine events are kept. There is no rollup tier — these are discrete facts, so rows simply age out. Lowering it prunes existing rows.
